field.label: Add to Cart from Listing Page
field.comment: Show the Add to Cart button on the product tiles of category listings, search results and product widgets. When disabled the tiles only link to the product page; the product page keeps its own button.

field.label: Terms & Conditions CMS Page Identifier
field.comment: CMS page identifier for the Terms of Service link in the footer.

field.label: Privacy Policy CMS Page Identifier
field.comment: CMS page identifier for the Privacy Policy link in the footer.

field.label: Generate a missing meta description
field.comment: A category, product or CMS page without a meta description (and no store default) gets one made from its own description, short description or content: tags removed, cut at a word boundary within 160 characters. A value typed in the admin is never replaced.

field.label: Rate Limit Search and Filter Requests
field.comment: Counts the requests that reach PHP (Varnish hits are free) per client address in 10 second windows and answers HTTP 429 Too Many Requests above the limits below.

field.label: Search Requests per 10 Seconds
field.comment: Budget of one client for the search suggestions (hyperion/search/suggest) and, counted separately, for the search results page. 0 disables the limit.

field.label: Filter Requests per 10 Seconds
field.comment: Budget of one client for layered navigation requests (hyperion/category/filter and category pages with filter or unknown parameters). 0 disables the limit.

field.label: Trusted Proxy Addresses
field.comment: Addresses of the reverse proxies in front of PHP (Varnish, the TLS terminator), one per line or comma separated. The client address is then read from X-Forwarded-For (rightmost address that is not a proxy). Leave empty when PHP sees the clients directly: the header is then ignored. Empty behind a proxy on a private network, the client is the forwarded address left after skipping the http_cache_hosts of env.php and at most one more hop in the proxy's subnet: a best effort that guesses the topology, so set the proxies in production.
